svg.title: The three-leg identity chain, and where each leg fails
svg.desc: Reaching Dataverse app-only takes three token exchanges, not one. Leg one: the Function requests a managed identity token whose audience is the token exchange audience api colon slash slash AzureADTokenExchange. Sovereign clouds use a different audience value, and getting it wrong fails at runtime rather than at deployment. Leg two: that token is presented as a client assertion on the app registration's client credentials request, returning an app-only token with no client secret involved. The federated credential's subject must be the managed identity's object or principal ID, not its client ID; Entra accepts the wrong value silently and the failure surfaces later as a failed token exchange. Leg three: the app-only token calls the environment listing API and each environment's Dataverse Web API. The environment listing scope contains a double slash that is not a typo, and the Power Apps Service resource principal must exist in the tenant, which in many tenants it never has been. Below the three legs, one step cannot be automated: a service principal cannot register itself as a Power Platform management application, so one interactive administrator sign-in is required the first time.
svg.text: The identity chain is three parties, not one
“Managed identity, so no secrets” is true, and it is not the whole story.

g.text: The Function requests a managed identity token whose audience is the token-exchange audience.
Fails when: a sovereign cloud uses a different audience. Surfaces at runtime, not at deployment.
That token becomes a client assertion, returning an app-only token. No client secret exists anywhere.
Fails when: the federated credential's subject is the client ID instead of the object ID. Entra accepts it silently.
App token → Power Platform and Dataverse
Lists every environment, then reads each environment's Web API using that organization's URL as the scope.
Fails when: the listing scope's double slash is “corrected”, or the Power Apps Service principal was never provisioned.
